tb21_profile.skill: Wire a push-to-deploy chain by hand: create a bare repo reachable over SSH, write a post-receive hook that checks the tree out into a webroot, and get an HTTP server serving that directory on a fixed port, verified end to end with curl
tb21_profile.domain: Git server administration (bare repos, hooks, worktree checkout) plus Unix web-server setup (nginx/apache/http.server) and SSH
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service: multi-component integration validated by a functional end-to-end request

tools.py search tmax 'git hook|post-receive|when a new .{0,30} is pushed|whenever .{0,30} pushed|bare repositor|git server' -n 30
tools.py words tmax post-receive checkout worktree 8080 http -n 25

Socket creation fails from the address configuration, so the server never listens; the exact failure a misconfigured webserver shows.
Server will not start with default settings; diagnosing why an HTTP server fails to come up and listen.
CLI mishandles host-only or port-only endpoint configuration; listen-address configuration parsing.
Unix socket files not unlinked on close, so a restart cannot rebind; the stale-socket failure a redeploy hook hits.
Arbiter socket unlinking inverted on shutdown; same stop-then-restart-the-listener problem a deploy hook must handle.
Server configuration loading broken; getting the server to actually apply the config file you wrote.
X-Forwarded-For handling broken; reverse-proxy header plumbing between a front server and its backend.
GZip middleware not applying to responses; the HTTP response pipeline that delivers served content.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Repo.reset_index is broken; materialising a commit's tree into a working directory is exactly what a post-receive checkout does.
porcelain.add corrupts the branch and status reports nonsense; repository and ref state after a write, the thing a push mutates.
Config parsing breaks when cloning a local repository by path; clone-from-a-server-path is the client step here.
Tracking-branch entries in .git/config parsed wrongly; remote and branch configuration semantics behind `git push origin master`.
Environment passed to clone_from is not retained in the resulting repo; remote configuration persistence after a clone.
Cannot pass environment variables to git subprocesses needed for commit/commit-tree; the same env-for-git problem hooks hit.
Adding files breaks for a repo rooted at the filesystem root; absolute-path handling inside a repository.
send_file silently unpacks gzipped files; serving a file from disk with the bytes the client expected.
204 response emits a Transfer-Encoding header against RFC 7230; emitting a well-formed HTTP response from a server you run.
Response splitting via status line and header names; HTTP server response hygiene, weakly related to configuring one.

notes: TMax owns this one: 154 of its instructions set up a bare repo with a post-receive hook, and roughly a dozen combine that with nginx/HTTP on a fixed port and a curl-based acceptance check. Those are near-duplicates of the TB2.1 task and the retrievers surfaced almost none of them (the shortlist was dominated by 'hello world' and generic nginx tasks); I found them with a post-receive/bare-repository regex and a 'post-receive checkout worktree 8080 http' word query. TerminalWorld has no git-server tasks at all but has strong isolated halves: push-index.html-to-a-bare-remote, and make-a-web-server-actually-serve-its-docroot-on-a-port. RTS's git pool is mostly 'mdlr import from a bare repo' boilerplate (~200 near-identical instructions) which I discounted; what survives is push-to-a-bare-remote and Apache-document-root tasks. For the SWE corpora I split the domain: gunicorn/daphne/starlette cover bind-a-server-to-a-port and serve-a-static-file, dulwich/GitPython cover the repository and checkout internals a post-receive hook depends on.
